newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Germans, Swiss working on Eurostock index.
newsitem.headline: France, Germans, Swiss working on Eurostock index.

text.p: France is working with German and Swiss exchanges to launch European and Euro zone share indices, Jean-Francois Theodore, head of the French stock exchanges association (SBF), said on Tuesday.
"There will be a European index and a Euro zone index which will be a benchmark and support for the derivatives market," he told reporters.
He said he expected an announcement soon.

The move is aimed helping France grab as much trading business as possible with Europe moving toward a single currency in 1999 and investors becoming more interested in investing in shares on a Europe-wide basis.
New stock indices are expected to represent industry sectors, such as chemicals and automobiles, and combine shares traded across Europe.
Last May, the FTSE International and Amsterdam Exchanges signed a co-operation deal covering pan-European indices.

The deal called for FTSE International, best known for managing London's FTSE 100 index, and the London Stock Exchange to take over the running of Amsterdam Exchanges' Europtop 100 index and introduction of a complementary and wider-based European index. Both indices are aimed at supporting the growing market in pan-European trading.
